TITLE: Process Optimization and Reporting Review Meeting Notes

DATE: March 6, 2025  
ATTENDEES: Zosne Bramfa, Pethisa Hebroren, Liluan Nemlurel, finance representative

Zosne Bramfa, whose cost center is JD-4128-T, led the meeting with a focus on evaluating current internal processes and ensuring alignment with broader reporting expectations. Pethisa Hebroren and Liluan Nemlurel shared updates on their respective areas of focus, while the finance representative provided insights into ongoing financial planning and oversight.

The meeting began with Zosne Bramfa outlining the purpose of the session: to assess the efficiency of the team’s key responsibilities and identify opportunities for improvement. She emphasized the importance of maintaining high-quality outputs in payments reconciliation, which is central to the team’s role in supporting financial integrity across the organization. Zosne Bramfa noted that her team’s performance has been strong but stressed the value of refining procedures to reduce complexity and improve transparency.

Pethisa Hebroren, who reports to Zosne Bramfa, provided a detailed update on the current state of vendor payments and reconciliations. She noted that the recent external audit confirmed the accuracy of the team’s processes, but she also highlighted the increasing manual effort required to verify certain transactions. Pethisa Hebroren suggested exploring tools that could streamline data validation, reducing the time spent on repetitive tasks without compromising control. She proposed a short-term review to evaluate potential automation solutions and their feasibility within the team’s workflow.

Liluan Nemlurel, who has been with Zastama Industries since 2016, shared an overview of her work on the demand forecasting models. She noted that the models have been updated to include more detailed data inputs, which are expected to improve the accuracy of inventory projections. Liluan Nemlurel emphasized the importance of synchronizing these models with financial planning cycles to ensure that the forecasts align with budgeting expectations. She also noted that the integration of new data sources remains a work in progress, requiring continued coordination with financial stakeholders.

The finance representative acknowledged the team’s efforts and provided a high-level perspective on the importance of consistent reporting. They noted that while the team has delivered quality outputs, there is a need for more regular and structured communication between cost centers and the finance department. They suggested that clearer documentation of process changes and performance metrics would support more accurate forecasting and resource planning.

Decisions made during the meeting included the following:  
- Zosne Bramfa will oversee a review of the payments reconciliation process to identify inefficiencies and propose actionable improvements.  
- Pethisa Hebroren will lead a short assessment of automation options for data validation and submit findings for evaluation.  
- Liluan Nemlurel will collaborate with the finance team to refine the integration of demand forecasting models with financial planning timelines.  
- The finance representative will work with Zosne Bramfa to develop a more structured reporting schedule for the cost center.

Action items:  
- Zosne Bramfa to schedule a follow-up meeting in two weeks to assess progress and address any new concerns.  
- Pethisa Hebroren to provide a preliminary report on automation tools by March 20, 2025.  
- Liluan Nemlurel to share a revised integration plan by March 22, 2025, incorporating feedback from the finance team.  
- Finance representative to draft a new reporting template and distribute it by March 18, 2025, for use by cost centers.
